sanskrit: tvaṁ soma pra cikito manīṣā tvaṁ rajiṣṭham anu neṣi panthām | tava praṇītī pitaro na indo deveṣu ratnam abhajanta dhīrāḥ ||
english: Thou, O Soma, art made known by wisdom; thou guidest us along the most direct path. By thy guidance, O Indu, the wise fathers obtained their share of treasure among the gods.

sanskrit: tvaṁ soma kratubhiḥ sukratur bhūs tvaṁ dakṣaiḥ sudakṣo viśvavedāḥ | tvaṁ vṛṣā vṛṣatvebhir mahitvā dyumnebhir dyumny abhavo nṛcakṣāḥ ||
english: Thou, O Soma, hast become of excellent resolve through thy powers of will; through thy capacities, all-knowing and of surpassing skill. Thou, the bull, by thy bull-like greatness, hast become resplendent through thy glories, O thou who seest men.

sanskrit: rājño nu te varuṇasya vratāni bṛhad gabhīraṁ tava soma dhāma | śuciṣ ṭvam asi priyo na mitro dakṣāyyo aryamevāsi soma ||
english: Thy ordinances are even as those of King Varuṇa; great and profound is thy dwelling, O Soma. Thou art pure, beloved like Mitra; thou art as fit for worship as Aryaman, O Soma.

sanskrit: yā te dhāmāni divi yā pṛthivyāṁ yā parvateṣv oṣadhīṣv apsu | tebhir no viśvaiḥ sumanā aheḻan rājan soma prati havyā gṛbhāya ||
english: With all those thy forms that are in heaven, that are on earth, that are on the mountains, in the plants, in the waters—with all of these, O King Soma, graciously and without anger receive our oblations.

sanskrit: tvaṁ somāsi satpatis tvaṁ rājota vṛtrahā | tvam bhadro asi kratuḥ ||
english: Thou, O Soma, art lord of the good; thou art king and also slayer of Vṛtra. Thou art the auspicious will.

sanskrit: tvaṁ ca soma no vaśo jīvātuṁ na marāmahe | priyastotro vanaspatiḥ ||
english: And thou, O Soma, at our wish we shall not die but live. Thou art the lord of the forest, dear to those who praise thee.

sanskrit: tvaṁ soma mahe bhagaṁ tvaṁ yūna ṛtāyate | dakṣaṁ dadhāsi jīvase ||
english: Thou, O Soma, grantest great good fortune; thou grantest power to the young man devoted to the sacred law. Thou bestowest strength that he may live.

sanskrit: tvaṁ naḥ soma viśvato rakṣā rājann aghāyataḥ | na riṣyet tvāvataḥ sakhā ||
english: Do thou, O Soma, O King, protect us from every side against him who would harm us. A friend who has thee as his protector shall not suffer hurt.

sanskrit: soma yās te mayobhuva ūtayaḥ santi dāśuṣe | tābhir no vitā bhava ||
english: O Soma, whatever blissful aids of thine exist for the worshipper—with all of those be thou our helper.

sanskrit: imaṁ yajñam idaṁ vaco jujuṣāṇa upāgahi | soma tvaṁ no vṛdhe bhava ||
english: Come near, delighting in this sacrifice and this hymn of praise. O Soma, be thou for our increase.

sanskrit: soma gīrbhiṣ ṭvā vayaṁ vardhayāmo vacovidaḥ | sumṛḻīko na ā viśa ||
english: We who are skilled in sacred words magnify thee, O Soma, with our songs. Enter into us with kindly grace.

sanskrit: gayasphāno amīvahā vasuvit puṣṭivardhanaḥ | sumitraḥ soma no bhava ||
english: O Soma, who art the sweller of homes, the dispeller of disease, the finder of wealth, the increaser of abundance—be thou a good ally to us.

sanskrit: soma rārandhi no hṛdi gāvo na yavaseṣv ā | marya iva sva okye ||
english: O Soma, make us content in heart, as cows are content in their pastures, as a young man in his own home.

sanskrit: yaḥ soma sakhye tava rāraṇad deva martyaḥ | taṁ dakṣaḥ sacate kaviḥ ||
english: The mortal, O Soma, O god, who delights in thy friendship—him wisdom follows as the seer's attendant.

sanskrit: uruṣyā ṇo abhiśasteḥ soma ni pāhy aṁhasaḥ | sakhā suśeva edhi naḥ ||
english: O Soma, protect us, rescue us from malediction, guard us from sin. Be to us a friend of beautiful grace.

sanskrit: ā pyāyasva sam etu te viśvataḥ soma vṛṣṇyam | bhavā vājasya saṁgathe ||
english: Wax full and mighty; let thy strength as a bull gather together unto thee from all sides, O Soma. Be present at the meeting-place of abundance.

sanskrit: ā pyāyasva madintama soma viśvebhir aṁśubhiḥ | bhavā naḥ suśravastamaḥ sakhā vṛdhe ||
english: Wax full, O most exhilarating Soma, with all thy streams. Be to us a most glorious friend for our growth.

sanskrit: saṁ te payāṁsi sam u yantu vājāḥ saṁ vṛṣṇyāny abhimātiṣāhaḥ | āpyāyamāno amṛtāya soma divi śravāṁsy uttamāni dhiṣva ||
english: Let thy milk-streams flow together, let thy food-prizes come together, let thy bull-powers that conquer the enemy come together, O Soma. Waxing full for immortality, fix thy highest glories in the sky.

sanskrit: yā te dhāmāni haviṣā yajanti tā te viśvā paribhūr astu yajñam | gayasphānaḥ prataraṇaḥ suvīro vīrahā pra carā soma duryān ||
english: Whatever of thy forms they worship with oblation—may all those of thee surround this sacrifice. O Soma, sweller of homes, guide onwards, rich in heroes, a man's leader; drive forward through the dwelling.

sanskrit: somo dhenuṁ somo arvantam āśuṁ somo vīraṁ karmaṇyaṁ dadāti | sādanyaṁ vidathyaṁ sabheya pitṛśravaṇaṁ yo dadāśad asmai ||
english: Soma gives the milk-cow, Soma gives the swift steed, Soma gives the hero fit for deeds—the sacrificial gift, the victor in assembly, worthy of the father's renown—to him who has offered to Soma.

sanskrit: aṣāḻhaṁ yutsu pṛtanāsu papriṁ svarṣām apsāṁ vṛjanasya gopām | bhareṣujāṁ sukṣitiṁ suśravasoṁ jayantaṁ tvām anu madema soma ||
english: Thee, the unconquerable in battles, the fulfiller in armies, the winner of the sun and waters, the herdsman of the settlement, born for the fight, of beautiful abode, of fair fame, the victorious—thee, O Soma, may we follow with joy.

sanskrit: tvam imā oṣadhīḥ soma viśvās tvam apo ajanayas tvaṁ gāḥ | tvam ā tatanthorv antarikṣaṁ tvaṁ jyotiṣā vi tamo vavartha ||
english: Thou, O Soma, hast generated all these plants; thou hast generated the waters; thou, the cows. Thou hast stretched out the wide mid-air; thou by thy light hast driven away the darkness.

sanskrit: devena no manasā deva soma rāyo bhāgaṁ sahasāvann abhi yudhya | mā tvā tanad īśiṣe vīryasyobhayebhyaḥ pra cikitsā gaviṣṭau ||
english: O divine Soma, with divine mind fight for our share of riches, O thou of a thousand powers. Let none deprive thee of lordship over thy might; discern well on both sides in the seeking of kine.

sanskrit: etā u tyā uṣasaḥ ketum akrata pūrve ardhe rajaso bhānum añjate | niṣkṛṇvānā āyudhānīva dhṛṣṇavaḥ prati gāvo ruṣīr yanti mātaraḥ ||
english: Lo, these Dawns have raised their signal; in the first half of the sky they anoint the sun. Bold, like those who polish their weapons, the ruddy cows, the mothers, advance to meet him.

sanskrit: ud apaptann aruṇā bhānavo vṛthā svāyujo aruṣīr gā ayukṣata | akrann uṣāso vayunāni pūrvathā ruśantam bhānum aruṣīr aśiśrayuḥ ||
english: The ruddy shining rays of Dawn flew freely upward; the self-yoked ruddy cows were harnessed. The Dawns have enacted their customs as of old; the ruddy ones have clung to the blazing sun.

sanskrit: arcanti nārīr apaso na viṣṭibhiḥ samānena yojanena parāvataḥ | iṣaṁ vahantīḥ sukṛte sudānave viśved aha yajamānāya sunvate ||
english: Like craftswomen at their tasks, they gleam from afar, all yoked together with one harnessing. Bearing food to the generous patron, to the well-doing sacrificer, all days they shine for the soma-presser.

sanskrit: adhi peśāṁsi vapate nṛtūr ivāporṇute vakṣa usreva barjaham | jyotir viśvasmai bhuvanāya kṛṇvatī gāvo na vrajaṁ vy uṣā avar tamaḥ ||
english: She puts on her adornments like a dancer; she uncovers her breast like a nursing mother. Creating light for all the world, Dawn, like cows streaming to their pen, has driven away the darkness.

sanskrit: praty arcī ruśad asyā adarśi vi tiṣṭhate bādhate kṛṣṇam abhvam | svaruṁ na peśo vidatheṣv añjañ citraṁ divo duhitā bhānum aśret ||
english: The shining flame of her was seen facing us; she spreads forth, pushing back the monstrous darkness. Blazing her ornament in the assemblies like a beam of light, the daughter of the sky has mounted the bright sunbeam.

sanskrit: atāriṣma tamasas pāram asyoṣā ucchantī vayunā kṛṇoti | śriye chando na smayate vibhātī supratīkā saumanasāyājīgaḥ ||
english: We have crossed to the farther shore of this darkness; Dawn as she shines makes the paths visible. Smiling for splendour like a verse of beauty, the fair-faced Dawn has aroused herself for our well-being.

sanskrit: bhāsvatī netrī sūnṛtānāṁ divaḥ stave duhitā gotamebhiḥ | prajāvato nṛvato aśvabudhyān uṣo goagrām̐ upa māsi vājān ||
english: Bright-shining guide of gracious words, daughter of the sky, thou art praised by the Gotamas. O Uṣas, bring near to us the prizes led by cows, whose vanguard is rich in men, whose foundation is horses.

sanskrit: uṣas tam aśyāṁ yaśasaṁ suvīraṁ dāsapravargaṁ rayim aśvabudhyam | sudaṁsasā śravasā yā vibhāsi vājaprasūtā subhage bṛhantam ||
english: O Dawn, may I obtain that glorious wealth, rich in fine heroes, surpassing in servants, grounded in horses. O thou of beautiful deeds, thou who shinest with fame, O fortunate one who sets the prizes in motion, grant me the great bounty.

sanskrit: viśvāni devī bhuvanābhicakṣyā pratīcī cakṣur urviyā vi bhāti | viśvaṁ jīvaṁ carase bodhayantī viśvasya vācam avidan manāyoḥ ||
english: The goddess, seeing all the worlds face to face, shines broadly with her wide-turned eye. Arousing all living things to movement, she has found the speech of all beings in both minds.

sanskrit: punaḥ-punar jāyamānā purāṇī samānaṁ varṇam abhi śumbhamānā | śvaghnīva kṛtnur vija āminānā martasya devī jarayanty āyuḥ ||
english: Born again and again, ancient, adorning herself with the same colour, the goddess wastes away a mortal's life-span, like a skilled dice-player scattering the pieces.

sanskrit: vyūrṇvatī divo antām abodhy apa svasāraṁ sanutar yuyoti | praminatī manuṣyā yugāni yoṣā jārasya cakṣasā vi bhāti ||
english: Uncovering the ends of the sky she has awakened; she drives her sister far away. She who diminishes the generations of men, the maiden shines with the glance of a lover.

sanskrit: paśūn na citrā subhagā prathānā sindhur na kṣoda urviyā vy aśvait | aminatī daivyāni vratāni sūryasya ceti raśmibhir dṛśānā ||
english: Brilliant and fortunate, spreading herself out like herds of cattle, like a river's stream she has moved widely. Not violating the divine ordinances, she of the sun's rays has come forth to be seen.

sanskrit: uṣas tac citram ā bharāsmabhyaṁ vājinīvati | yena tokaṁ ca tanayaṁ ca dhāmahe ||
english: O Uṣas, bring to us that brilliant bounty, O thou who art rich in prize-horses, whereby we may sustain both offspring and descendants.

sanskrit: uṣo adyeha gomaty aśvāvati vibhāvari | revad asme vy uccha sūnṛtāvati ||
english: O Uṣas, shine forth here today, rich in kine, rich in horses, richly shining, full of gracious gifts, for us with radiance.

sanskrit: yukṣvā hi vājinīvaty aśvām̐ adyāruṇām̐ uṣaḥ | athā no viśvā saubhagāny ā vaha ||
english: For thou art rich in prizes, O Uṣas; yoke today thy ruddy horses. Then bring to us all good fortunes.

sanskrit: aśvinā vartir asmad ā gomad dasrā hiraṇyavat | arvāg rathaṁ samanasā ni yacchatam ||
english: O Aśvins, bring your chariot near from us—the goal rich in cattle and gold, O wonder-working pair. Hold back your car with one mind toward us.

sanskrit: yāv itthā ślokam ā divo jyotir janāya cakrathuḥ | ā na ūrjaṁ vahatam aśvinā yuvam ||
english: Ye two who have thus made the light from the sky, the signal for mankind—bring to us strength, O ye two Aśvins.

sanskrit: eha devā mayobhuvā dasrā hiraṇyavartanī | uṣarbudho vahantu somapītaye ||
english: May the gods, blissful, wonder-workers, of golden path, who wake at Dawn, come hither and drive us to the drinking of Soma.

sanskrit: agnīṣomāv imaṁ su me śṛṇutaṁ vṛṣaṇā havam | prati sūktāni haryatam bhavataṁ dāśuṣe mayaḥ ||
english: O Agni and Soma, hear well this my invocation, ye two bulls. Accept the well-spoken hymns; be a comfort to the worshipper.

sanskrit: agnīṣomā yo adya vāṁ idaṁ vacaḥ saparyati | tasmai dhattaṁ suvīryaṁ gavāṁ poṣaṁ svaśvyam ||
english: O Agni and Soma, he who today serves you both with this word—grant him heroic power, increase of kine, abundance of horses.

sanskrit: agnīṣomā ya āhutiṁ yo vāṁ dāśād dhaviṣkṛtim | sa prajayā suvīryaṁ viśvam āyur vy aśnavat ||
english: O Agni and Soma, he who offers you an oblation, who presents you with the prepared offering—may he attain offspring, heroic power, and all-encompassing life.

sanskrit: agnīṣomā ceti tad vīryaṁ vāṁ yad amuṣṇītam avasam paṇiṁ gāḥ | avātiratam bṛsayasya śeṣo vindataṁ jyotir ekam bahubhyaḥ ||
english: O Agni and Soma, that heroic deed of yours is proclaimed whereby ye took away the cows from the niggardly Paṇi without shelter. Ye overcame the remnant of Bṛsaya; ye won one light for many.

sanskrit: yuvam etāni divi rocanāny agniś ca soma sakratū adhattam | yuvaṁ sindhūm̐r abhiśaster avadyād agnīṣomāv amuñcataṁ gṛbhītān ||
english: These two, Agni and Soma, of one purpose, set these luminaries in the sky. You two released the rivers seized by reproach and disgrace, O Agni and Soma.

sanskrit: ānyaṁ divo mātariśvā jabhārāmathnād anyam pari śyeno adreḥ | agnīṣomā brahmaṇā vāvṛdhānoruṁ yajñāya cakrathur u lokam ||
english: One Mātariśvan brought from the sky; the eagle shook the other loose from the rock. O Agni and Soma, waxing great through sacred prayer, ye made the broad world for the sacrifice.

sanskrit: agnīṣomā haviṣaḥ prasthi tasya vītaṁ haryataṁ vṛṣaṇā juṣethām | suśarmāṇā svavosā hi bhūtam athā dhattaṁ yajamānāya śaṁ yoḥ ||
english: O Agni and Soma, accept and enjoy the oblation that has been set forth; O ye bulls, be pleased with it. Be ye of beautiful shelter and good protection. Then grant to the sacrificer welfare and ease.

sanskrit: yo agnīṣomā haviṣā saparyād devadrīcā manasā yo ghṛtena | tasya vrataṁ rakṣatam pātam aṁhaso viśe janāya mahi śarma yacchatam ||
english: He who worships Agni and Soma with oblation, with god-directed mind and with ghee—protect his vow, guard him from sin, and grant great shelter to the people and the clan.

sanskrit: agnīṣomā savedasā sahūtī vanataṁ giraḥ | saṁ devatrā babhūvathuḥ ||
english: O Agni and Soma, rich in the same wealth, invoked together, favour our songs of praise. Ye two have come together in the divine realm.

sanskrit: agnīṣomāv anena vāṁ yo vāṁ ghṛtena dāśati | tasmai dīdayatam bṛhat ||
english: O Agni and Soma, he who presents to you both this offering of ghee—for him let the great light blaze forth.

sanskrit: agnīṣomāv imāni no yuvaṁ havyā jujoṣatam | ā yātam upa naḥ sacā ||
english: O Agni and Soma, may ye two together delight in these oblations of ours. Come near to us together.

sanskrit: agnīṣomā pipṛtam arvato na ā pyāyantām usriyā havyasūdaḥ | asme balāni maghawatsu dhattaṁ kṛṇutaṁ no adhvaraṁ śruṣṭimantam ||
english: O Agni and Soma, fill us as you would fill a horse; let the tawny morning cows, offerers of the oblation, swell. Place strength in us among the bountiful ones; make our sacrifice attentive to the call.

sanskrit: imaṁ stomam arhate jātavedase ratham iva sam mahemā manīṣayā | bhadrā hi naḥ pramatir asya saṁsady agne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṁ tava ||
english: We have built up this hymn of praise for Jātavedas as one builds a chariot with wisdom. For his guidance is good for us in this assembly. O Agni, may we never suffer harm in thy friendship.

sanskrit: yasmai tvam āyajase sa sādhaty anarvā kṣeti dadhate suvīryam | sa tūtāva nainam aśnoty aṁhatir agne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṁ tava ||
english: He for whom thou dost secure the sacrifice prospers; unchallenged he dwells, acquiring heroic power. Distress can never reach him, the oft-protected. O Agni, may we never suffer harm in thy friendship.

sanskrit: śakema tvā samidhaṁ sādhayā dhiyas tve devā havir adanty āhutam | tvam ādityām̐ ā vaha tān hy uśmasy agne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṁ tava ||
english: May we be able to kindle thee and accomplish our prayers. In thee the gods eat the oblation that has been offered. Bring the Ādityas hither, for them we desire. O Agni, may we never suffer harm in thy friendship.

sanskrit: bharāmedhmaṁ kṛṇavāmā havīṁṣi te citayantaḥ parvaṇā-parvaṇā vayam | jīvātave prataraṁ sādhayā dhiyo gne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṁ tava ||
english: We shall bring fuel and make oblations for thee, advancing through each sacred rite, being mindful. Accomplish our prayers for the prolonging of life. O Agni, may we never suffer harm in thy friendship.

sanskrit: viśāṁ gopā asya caranti jantavo dvipac ca yad uta catuṣpad aktubhiḥ | citraḥ praketa uṣaso mahām̐ asy agne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṁ tava ||
english: As herdsman of the clans, creatures move through the nights—those that walk on two feet and those on four. Thou art the brilliant signal of the Dawn, the great one. O Agni, may we never suffer harm in thy friendship.

sanskrit: tvam adhvaryur uta hotāsi pūrvyaḥ praśāstā potā januṣā purohitaḥ | viśvā vidvām̐ ārtwijyā dhīra puṣyasy agne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṁ tava ||
english: Thou art the adhvaryu and the ancient hotar; thou art the praśāstṛ, the potṛ, the purohita by birth. Wise one, thou dost flourish knowing all the priestly functions. O Agni, may we never suffer harm in thy friendship.

sanskrit: yo viśvataḥ supratīkaḥ sadṛṅṅ asi dūre cit san taḻid ivāti rocase | rātryāś cid andho ati deva paśyasy agne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṁ tava ||
english: Thou who art of beautiful aspect from every side, appearing alike everywhere; though far away thou shinest through like lightning. O god, thou seest through even the darkness of night. O Agni, may we never suffer harm in thy friendship.

sanskrit: pūrvo devā bhavatu sunvato ratho smākaṁ śaṁso abhy astu dūḍhyaḥ | tad ā jānītota puṣyatā vaco gne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṁ tava ||
english: Let the chariot of the soma-pressers be foremost of the gods; let our praise overcome the malicious. Know this and foster our word. O Agni, may we never suffer harm in thy friendship.

sanskrit: vadhair duḥśaṁsām̐ apa dūḍhyo jahi dūre vā ye anti vā ke cid atriṇaḥ | athā yajñāya gṛṇate sugaṁ kṛdhy agne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṁ tava ||
english: With thy missiles slay the evil-speakers, the malicious—whoever the devouring ones may be, near or far. Then make easy passage for the sacrificer who sings thy praise. O Agni, may we never suffer harm in thy friendship.

sanskrit: yad ayukthā aruṣā rohitā rathe vātajūtā vṛṣabhasye va te ravaḥ | ād invasi vanino dhūmaketonāgne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṁ tava ||
english: When thou hast yoked the ruddy, red horses to thy chariot, wind-driven, thy roar is like that of a bull. Then thou dost fill the forests with thy smoke-bannered flame. O Agni, may we never suffer harm in thy friendship.

sanskrit: adha svanād uta bibhyuḥ patatriṇo drapsā yat te yavasādo vy asthiran | sugaṁ tat te tāvakebhyo rathebhyo gne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṁ tava ||
english: Then even the winged birds are frightened by thy roar, when the sparks that feed upon the plants fly apart. May that passage be easy for thy chariots. O Agni, may we never suffer harm in thy friendship.

sanskrit: ayam mitrasya varuṇasya dhāyase vayātām marutāṁ heḻo adbhutaḥ | mṛḻā su no bhūtv eṣāṁ manaḥ punar agne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṁ tava ||
english: This Agni, the wondrous one, is to be nourished for Mitra and Varuṇa; may the wrath of the Maruts pass away. May their mind be gracious to us once more. O Agni, may we never suffer harm in thy friendship.

sanskrit: devo devānām asi mitro adbhuto vasur vasūnām asi cāruḥ adhvare | śarman syāma tava sapratha stame gne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṁ tava ||
english: Thou art a god of gods, the wondrous Mitra; thou art the wealth of the wealthy, beautiful at the rite. May we abide in thy shelter, most widely renowned. O Agni, may we never suffer harm in thy friendship.

sanskrit: tat te bhadraṁ yat samiddhaḥ sve dame somāhuto jarase mṛḻayattamaḥ | dadhāsi ratnaṁ draviṇaṁ ca dāśuṣe gne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṁ tava ||
english: That is auspicious for thee when, kindled in thy own home, fed with Soma, most merciful and ageless, thou bestowest treasure and riches on the worshipper. O Agni, may we never suffer harm in thy friendship.

sanskrit: yasmai tvaṁ sudraviṇo dadāśo nāgāstvam adite sarvatātā | yam bhadreṇa śavasā codayāsi prajāvatā rādhasā te syāma ||
english: He to whom thou, rich in wealth, hast given freely, him thou dost make sinless and whole, O Aditi. He whom thou dost impel with auspicious strength—may we be among those blessed with offspring and thy bounty.

sanskrit: sa tvam agne saubhagatvasya vidvān asmākam āyuḥ pra tireha deva | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: So do thou, O Agni, knowing the nature of good fortune, prolong our life here, O god. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Sky grant us this.

sanskrit: dve virūpe carataḥ svarthe anyānyā vatsam upa dhāpayete | harir anyasyām bhavati svadhāvāñ chukro anyasyāṁ dadṛśe suvarcāḥ ||
english: Two beings of different form move toward the same goal, and each suckles a calf in turn. One is tawny, possessing inherent power, in one; in the other a bright one of beautiful radiance has appeared.

sanskrit: daśemaṁ tvaṣṭur janayanta garbham atandrāso yuvatayo vibhṛtram | tigmānīkaṁ svayaśasaṁ janeṣu virocamānam pari ṣīṁ nayanti ||
english: Ten untiring young women gave birth to this embryo of Tvaṣṭṛ, this widely carried one. They lead him around among the people, sharp-edged, self-glorious, shining radiantly.

sanskrit: trīṇi jānā pari bhūṣanty asya samudra ekaṁ divy ekam apsu | pūrvām anu pra diśam pārthivānām ṛtūn praśāsad vi dadhāv anuṣṭhu ||
english: Three races tend to him; one ocean is his, one in the sky, one in the waters. Following the former direction of earthly beings, he ordains the seasons and distributes them in due order.

sanskrit: ka imaṁ vo niṇyam ā ciketa vatso mātṝr janayata svadhābhiḥ | bahvīnāṁ garbho apasām upasthān mahān kavir niś carati svadhāvān ||
english: Who among you has perceived this secret? The calf has generated the mothers by his own powers. The embryo of many active ones, dwelling in their lap, the great seer wanders forth by night, possessed of inherent power.

sanskrit: āviṣṭyo vardhate cāruḥ āsu jihmānām ūrdhvaḥ svayaśā upasthe | ubhe tvaṣṭur bibhyatur jāyamānāt pratīcī siṁham prati joṣayete ||
english: Entering in, the beautiful one grows upright on the lap of the crooked ones, of self-glory. Both consorts of Tvaṣṭṛ tremble at his birth; they who face away turn toward the lion with joy.

sanskrit: ubhe bhadre joṣayete na mene gāvo na vāśrā upa tasthuhr evaiḥ | sa dakṣāṇāṁ dakṣapatir babhūvāñjanti yaṁ dakṣiṇato havirbhiḥ ||
english: Both benefit from him, deeming nothing; the lowing cows have come near by his paths. He has become lord of the capable among the skilful; they anoint him with oblations on the right side.

sanskrit: ud yaṁyamīti saviteva bāhū ubhe sicau yatate bhīma ṛñjan | uc chukram atkaṁ ajate simasmān navā mātṛbhyo vasanā jahāti ||
english: He stretches both arms upward like Savitṛ; terrible, blazing, he strains on both sides of the channel. He drives the bright garment upward from himself; he sheds new garments for the mothers.

sanskrit: tveṣaṁ rūpaṁ kṛṇuta uttaraṁ yat sampṛñcānaḥ sadane gobhir adbhiḥ | kavir budhnam pari marmṛjyate dhīḥ sā devatātā samitir babhūva ||
english: He makes his form most fierce when he mingles in his seat with the cows and waters. The inspired one polishes the foundation; that meeting of divine powers has come into being.

sanskrit: uru te jrayaḥ pary eti budhnaṁ virocamānam mahiṣasya dhāma | viśvebhir agne svayaśobhir iddho dabdhebhiḥ pāyubhiḥ pāhy asmān ||
english: Thy wide expanse goes around the foundation, the dwelling-place of the great buffalo shining forth. O Agni, kindled with all thine own glories, guard us with thy inviolable protections.

sanskrit: dhanvan srotaḥ kṛṇute gātum ūrmiṁ śukrair ūrmibhir abhi nakṣati kṣām | viśvā sanāni jaṭhareṣu dhatte ntar navāsu carati prasūṣu ||
english: In the desert he makes a watercourse, a way, a wave; with bright waves he approaches the earth. He holds all the prizes in his belly; within, he moves in the new birth-waters.

sanskrit: evā no agne samidhā vṛdhāno revat pāvaka śravase vi bhāhi | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: Thus, O Agni, waxing great by fuel, O Purifier, shine forth brilliantly for our fame. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Sky grant us this.

sanskrit: sa pratnathā sahasā jāyamānaḥ sadyaḥ kāvyāni baḻ adhatta viśvā | āpaś ca mitraṁ dhiṣaṇā ca sādhan devā agniṁ dhārayan draviṇodām ||
english: Born as of old with power, he straightway seized all the inspired wisdom. Accomplishing friendship with the waters and with Dhiṣaṇā, the gods sustained Agni, the giver of wealth.

sanskrit: sa pūrvayā nividā kavyatāyor imāḥ prajā ajanayan manūnām | vivasvatā cakṣasā dyām apaś ca devā agniṁ dhārayan draviṇodām ||
english: By the first invocation of the two inspired sages, he generated these offspring of Manu. With the eye of Vivasvat, both the sky and the waters—the gods sustained Agni, the giver of wealth.

sanskrit: tam īḻata prathamaṁ yajñasādhaṁ viśa ārīr āhutam ṛñjasānam | ūrjaḥ putram bharataṁ sṛpradānum devā agniṁ dhārayan draviṇodām ||
english: Him they praised as the first accomplisher of the sacrifice, offering to the races of strangers, the gliding one. The son of vigour, Bharata, of flowing liberality—the gods sustained Agni, the giver of wealth.

sanskrit: sa mātariśvā puruvārapuṣṭir vidad gātuṁ tanayāya svarvit | viśāṁ gopā janitā rodasyor devā agniṁ dhārayan draviṇodām ||
english: He who is Mātariśvan, rich in many gifts, found the path for his son, winning the sun. The herdsman of the clans, generator of heaven and earth—the gods sustained Agni, the giver of wealth.

sanskrit: naktoṣāsā varṇam āmemyāne dhāpayete śiśum ekaṁ samīcī | dyāvākṣāmā rukmo antar vi bhāti devā agniṁ dhārayan draviṇodām ||
english: Night and Dawn, assuming the same colour, both suckle the one child as they face each other. The golden one gleams between heaven and earth—the gods sustained Agni, the giver of wealth.

sanskrit: rāyo budhnaḥ saṁgamano vasūnāṁ yajñasya ketur manmasādhano veḥ | amṛtatvaṁ rakṣamāṇāsa enaṁ devā agniṁ dhārayan draviṇodām ||
english: The foundation of riches, the meeting-place of goods, the banner of the sacrifice, the accomplisher of prayer and bird—those who guard immortality, the gods sustained Agni, the giver of wealth.

sanskrit: nū ca purā ca sadanaṁ rayīṇāṁ jātasya ca jāyamānasya ca kṣām | sataś ca gopām bhavataś ca bhūrer devā agniṁ dhārayan draviṇodām ||
english: Now and of old the seat of riches, the earth of what is born and what is being born, the herdsman of what exists and what will be abundant—the gods sustained Agni, the giver of wealth.

sanskrit: draviṇodā draviṇasas turasya draviṇodāḥ sanarasya pra yaṁsat | draviṇodā vīravatīm iṣaṁ no draviṇodā rāsate dīrgham āyuḥ ||
english: The wealth-giver—may he advance the wealth of the swift; the wealth-giver of the munificent man. The wealth-giver shall grant us food rich in heroes; the wealth-giver shall bestow long life.

sanskrit: evā no agne samidhā vṛdhāno revat pāvaka śravase vi bhāhi | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: Thus, O Agni, waxing great by fuel, O Purifier, shine forth brilliantly for our fame. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Sky grant us this.

sanskrit: apa naḥ śośucad agham agne śuśugdhy ā rayim | apa naḥ śośucad agham ||
english: O Agni, burn away our sin; shine thou and bring us wealth. Burn away our sin.

sanskrit: sukṣetriyā sugātuyā vasūyā ca yajāmahe | apa naḥ śośucad agham ||
english: We worship for good land, for easy passage, and for goods. Burn away our sin.

sanskrit: pra yad bhandiṣṭha eṣāṁ prāsmākāsaś ca sūrayaḥ | apa naḥ śośucad agham ||
english: When the most glorious among them and our own patrons shine forth—burn away our sin.

sanskrit: pra yat te agne sūrayo jāyemahi pra te vayam | apa naḥ śośucad agham ||
english: When through thee, O Agni, thy patrons prevail, when we too prevail—burn away our sin.

sanskrit: pra yad agneḥ sahasvato viśvato yanti bhānavaḥ | apa naḥ śośucad agham ||
english: When the rays of Agni the mighty go forth from everywhere—burn away our sin.

sanskrit: tvaṁ hi viśvatomukha viśvataḥ paribhūr asi | apa naḥ śośucad agham ||
english: For thou art the one whose face turns to all sides, thou art the one who surrounds from every side—burn away our sin.

sanskrit: dviṣo no viśvatomukhāti nāveva pāraya | apa naḥ śośucad agham ||
english: O thou whose face turns to all sides, carry us past our foes like a boat—burn away our sin.

sanskrit: sa naḥ sindhum iva nāvayāti parṣā svastaye | apa naḥ śośucad agham ||
english: May he carry us safely across like a ferry-boat over a river, to well-being—burn away our sin.

sanskrit: vaiśvānarasya sumatau syāma rājā hi kaṁ bhuvanānām abhiśrīḥ | ito jāto viśvam idaṁ vi caṣṭe vaiśvānaro yatate sūryeṇa ||
english: May we be in the grace of Vaiśvānara, for he is the resplendent king of all the worlds. Born from here, he surveys this whole universe; Vaiśvānara strives together with the sun.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭo divi pṛṣṭo agniḥ pṛthivyām pṛṣṭo viśvā oṣadhīr ā viveśa | vaiśvānaraḥ sahasā pṛṣṭo agniḥ sa no divā sa riṣaḥ pātu naktam ||
english: Questioned in heaven, questioned in earth, Agni has entered into all the plants. Vaiśvānara, Agni questioned with power—may he protect us from injury by day and by night.

sanskrit: vaiśvānara tava tat satyam astv asmān rāyo maghavānaḥ sacantām | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: O Vaiśvānara, may that be true for thee; may bountiful riches attend us. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Sky grant us this.

sanskrit: jātavedase sunavāma somaṁ arātīyato ni dahāti vedaḥ | sa naḥ parṣad ati durgāṇi viśvā nāveva sindhuṁ duritāty agniḥ ||
english: We press Soma for Jātavedas; his knowledge burns down those who harbour ill will. May Agni carry us past all difficult places, across all evil paths, as a boat carries one across a river.

sanskrit: sa yo vṛṣā vṛṣṇyebhiḥ samokā maho divaḥ pṛthivyāś ca samrāṭ | satīnasatvā havyo bhareṣu marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ||
english: He who is the bull dwelling together with his bull-powers, the sovereign lord of the great sky and the earth, of truly heroic strength, to be invoked in battles—may Indra with the Maruts be for our aid.

sanskrit: yasyānāptaḥ sūryasyeva yāmo bhare-bhare vṛtrahā śuṣmo asti | vṛṣantamaḥ sakhibhiḥ svebhir evair marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ||
english: Whose unimpeded course is like the sun's, whose Vṛtra-slaying fierceness exists in every battle, who is most bull-like with his own friends and companions—may Indra with the Maruts be for our aid.

sanskrit: divo na yasya retaso dughānāḥ panthāso yanti śavasāparītāḥ | taraddveṣāḥ sāsahiḥ pauṁsyebhir marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ||
english: Whose paths go forth like those yielding the seed of heaven, filled with power, who by his manly deeds pierces through enmities as one who has conquered—may Indra with the Maruts be for our aid.

sanskrit: so aṅgirobhir aṅgirastamo bhūd vṛṣā vṛṣabhiḥ sakhibhiḥ sakhā san | ṛgmibhir ṛgmī gātubhir jyeṣṭho marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ||
english: He became most Aṅgiras-like with the Aṅgirasas, a bull with the bulls, a companion with companions; most hymn-rich with the hymn-singers, the eldest in the ways—may Indra with the Maruts be for our aid.

sanskrit: sa sūnubhir na rudrebhir ṛbhvā nṛṣāhye sāsahvām̐ amitrān | sanīḻebhiḥ śravasyāni tūrvan marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ||
english: Skilful like the Rudras, his sons, having overcome his foes in the trial of men's strength, winning glorious deeds with his nest-companions—may Indra with the Maruts be for our aid.

sanskrit: sa manyumīḥ samadanasya kartāsmākebhir nṛbhiḥ sūryaṁ sanat | asminn ahan satpatiḥ puruhūto marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ||
english: He the wrathful one who brings about the conflict, who has won the sun through our heroes, who on this day is the lord of the good, much-invoked—may Indra with the Maruts be for our aid.

sanskrit: tam ūtayo raṇayañ chūrasātau taṁ kṣemasya kṣitayaḥ kṛṇvata trām | sa viśvasya karuṇasyeśa eko marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ||
english: His aids delight in the winning of heroes in battle; the clans of settled land make him their protector. He alone is lord of all that is pitiable—may Indra with the Maruts be for our aid.

sanskrit: tam apsanta śavasa utsaveṣu naro naram avase taṁ dhanāya | so andhe cit tamasi jyotir vidan marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ||
english: Men have longed for him of great strength at the festivals, man craving man for his aid and for wealth. Even in blind darkness he finds the light—may Indra with the Maruts be for our aid.

sanskrit: sa savyena yamati vrādhataś cit sa dakṣiṇe saṁgṛbhītā kṛtāni | sa kīriṇā cit sanitā dhanāni marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ||
english: With his left hand he restrains even the strong; in his right hand are gathered his achievements. Even with a weak man he wins riches—may Indra with the Maruts be for our aid.

sanskrit: sa grāmebhiḥ sanitā sa rathebhir vide viśvābhiḥ kṛṣṭibhir nv adya | sa pauṁsyebhir abhibhūr aśastīr marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ||
english: He shall win with the battle-hosts, shall win with the chariots; he is known today with all the peoples. By manly deeds he overcomes reproaches—may Indra with the Maruts be for our aid.

sanskrit: sa jāmibhir yat samajāti mīḻhe jāmibhir vā puruhūta evaiḥ | apāṁ tokasya tanayasya jeṣe marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ||
english: Whether in the assembly he meets with kindred or with non-kindred, O much-invoked, by his paths he wins offspring of the waters and descendants—may Indra with the Maruts be for our aid.

sanskrit: sa vajrabhṛd dasyuhā bhīma ugraḥ sahasracetāḥ śatanītha ṛbhvā | camrīṣo na śavasā pāñcajanyo marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ||
english: He who bears the thunderbolt, the slayer of Dasyus, terrible, fierce, of a thousand insights, of a hundredfold might, skilful—mighty as the bison of the five peoples—may Indra with the Maruts be for our aid.

sanskrit: tasya vajraḥ krandati smat svarṣā divo na tveṣo ravathaḥ śimīvān | taṁ sacante sanayas taṁ dhanāni marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ||
english: His thunderbolt always roars, winning the sun; his tumult is terrible, blazing as the sky. Ancient gifts attend him, riches attend him—may Indra with the Maruts be for our aid.

sanskrit: yasyājasraṁ śavasā mānam uktham paribhujad rodasī viśvataḥ sīm | sa pāriṣat kratubhir mandasāno marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ||
english: He whose ceaseless praise and proclamation with power fills heaven and earth on every side—may he, exhilarated by his powers of will, bring us through—may Indra with the Maruts be for our aid.

sanskrit: na yasya devā devatā na martā āpaś cana śavaso ntam āpuḥ | sa prarikvā tvakṣasā kṣmo divaś ca marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ||
english: Neither the gods and divine powers, nor mortals, nor even the waters have reached the limit of his might. He, the wandering one, with his skill fills both earth and sky—may Indra with the Maruts be for our aid.

sanskrit: rohic chyāvā sumadaṁśur lalāmīr dyukṣā rāya ṛjrāśvasya | vṛṣaṇvantam bibhratī dhūrṣu rathaṁ mandrā ciketa nāhuṣīṣu vikṣu ||
english: The ruddy-and-dark dappled mare, of beautiful bite, wearing ornaments, belonging to the celestial wealth of Ṛjrāśva—she, the pleasant one, bearing a bull-led chariot in the yoke-teams, has been seen among the Nahuṣa folk.

sanskrit: etat tyat ta indra vṛṣṇa ukthaṁ vārṣāgirā abhi gṛṇanti rādhaḥ | ṛjrāśvaḥ praṣṭibhir ambarīṣaḥ sahadevaḥ bhayamānaḥ surādhāḥ ||
english: This is indeed that praise of thine, O bull Indra, the bounty which the Vārṣāgiras celebrate. Ṛjrāśva with yoked teams, Ambarīṣa, Sahadevas, Bhayamāna, Surādhās—these sing thee.

sanskrit: dasyūñ chimyūm̐ś ca puruhūta evair hatvā pṛthivyāṁ śarvā ni barhīt | sanat kṣetraṁ sakhibhiḥ śvitnyebhiḥ sanat sūryaṁ sanad apaḥ suvajraḥ ||
english: Having slain the Dasyus and the Śimyus by his paths, O much-invoked one, Śarva has crushed them into the earth. He of the good thunderbolt won the field with white companions, won the sun, won the waters.

sanskrit: viśvāhendro adhivaktā no stv aparihvṛtāḥ sanuyāma vājam | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: May Indra be our advocate every day; unchecked, may we win the prize. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Sky grant us this.
